2	
3	> For teams using Helix in their apps. If you're contributing to Helix itself, read `contributor-ai/CONTRIBUTOR.md` instead.
4	
5	## What is Helix?
6	
7	A design system built for teams building AI-powered products. Components have explicit contracts,
8	predictable token structure, and machine-readable documentation.
9	
10	## Available packages
11	
12	| Package               | Purpose                              | Install                         |
13	|-----------------------|--------------------------------------|----------------------------------|
14	| `@helixds/react`      | All UI components                    | `pnpm add @helixds/react`       |
15	| `@helixds/tokens`    | CSS tokens + TypeScript constants    | `pnpm add @helixds/tokens`     |
16	
17	Icons are [Tabler Icons](https://tabler.io/icons) (`@tabler/icons-react`, a peer dependency of core),
18	always rendered through core's `Icon` component or a component's `icon` prop — never as a raw
19	`<IconXxx />` tag.
20	
21	## Data Analytics
22	
23	For metrics and data visualisation, use Helix's `Chart` component. It is the only supported chart renderer
24	and is branded through Apache ECharts using Helix semantic tokens. Never import ECharts directly, pass raw
25	ECharts options, or introduce another chart library. Choose `variant="line"`, `"bar"`, `"stacked-bar"`,
26	`"donut"`, or `"timeline"` based on the reader's question; compose charts with Helix `Card`, `Table`,
27	`Badge`, and `Tooltip` rather than recreating those UI pieces inside a chart.
28	
29	## Setup (required, once)
30	
31	```tsx
32	// app/layout.tsx or main.tsx
33	import '@helixds/tokens/helix.css';   // CSS custom properties
34	import '@helixds/react/globals.css';   // Tailwind base + component styles
35	```
36	
37	## Component inventory
38	
39	Every component's current status (draft / beta / stable) is **computed**, not listed here — see
40	Storybook → **Status**, or `contracts/stability.json` (`pnpm verify:stable`, ADR-018). draft = exists and
41	works; beta = passes all 8 automatic quality criteria; stable = beta + modeled in Figma.
42	
43	All components import from `@helixds/react`. Generated from `contracts/manifest.json` on every commit
44	(`pnpm docs:readme`) — do not edit the table by hand.
45	
46	<!-- helix:component-inventory:start -->
47	| Component | Category | Purpose |
48	|---|---|---|
49	| `Accordion` | core | A single collapsible disclosure — a header that expands/collapses a panel of content, with no JS height measurement needed. |
50	| `AppShell` | layout | The top-level page shell — composes a SideNav, a TopBar, and the scrollable main content into one consistent full-height layout. |
51	| `Avatar` | core | Represents a person or entity as a small circular image or initials indicator — a table row, a nav footer, a comment author. |
52	| `AvatarGroup` | core | Shows several people or entities associated with the same record as a compact overlapping stack of Avatars, collapsing whatever doesn't fit into a '+N' count. |
53	| `Badge` | core | Communicates status, category labels, or counts in a compact, high-contrast capsule. |
54	| `Button` | core | Triggers an action or navigates to a destination when pressed by the user. |
55	| `Card` | core | Groups related content in a visually distinct, flat surface — a dashboard widget, a settings group, a gallery tile. |
56	| `Chart` | core | Visualizes a metric with a token-branded, accessible chart so people can understand trends, comparisons, composition, or events. |
57	| `Checkbox` | core | Lets users select one or more independent options from a set, or confirm a single binary choice. |
58	| `CheckboxGroup` | core | Lets users choose zero or more options from a small, visible set of independent choices. |
59	| `Chip` | core | Represents a compact selectable label for filters, categories, or short choices. |
60	| `ChipGroup` | core | Shows a small set of related chips side by side — categories, tags or applied filters — as one labelled group. |
61	| `FAB` | core | A single, prominent floating action reachable from anywhere in the current view — optionally expanding into 1-3 closely related actions via a speed-dial. |
62	| `Icon` | core | Communicates meaning, action, or status through a recognizable visual symbol. |
63	| `IconButton` | core | Triggers an action via a single icon, with no visible text label — a toolbar action, a row action, a close/dismiss control. |
64	| `Input` | core | Allows users to enter a single line of free-form text. |
65	| `Menu` | core | A Helix-styled, portaled popup listbox anchored to a trigger element — the internal primitive Select uses instead of a native <select> dropdown, and the foundation for any future popup list (Combobox, a context menu, a DatePicker's own internals). |
66	| `Modal` | core | A centered overlay that interrupts the page for a focused task or decision — blocks interaction with the rest of the page until dismissed. |
67	| `MultiSelect` | core | Lets users choose several values from a predefined list, shown as removable chips inside the field. |
68	| `NavItem` | core | A single entry in a persistent navigation list (a SideNav, a tab rail) that links to another view. |
69	| `PageHeader` | layout | Introduces a page or major section: title, optional supporting description, and trailing actions in one consistent row. |
70	| `RadioButton` | core | A single radio input — the individual option unit RadioGroup renders per choice, exposed on its own for cases that need one radio outside a full group (e.g. |
71	| `RadioGroup` | core | Lets users choose exactly one option from a small, visible set of mutually exclusive choices. |
72	| `SegmentedControl` | core | Lets users switch between a small, fixed set of mutually exclusive modes or views, with no associated content panel. |
73	| `Select` | core | Lets users choose a single value from a predefined list. |
74	| `SideNav` | layout | The persistent vertical navigation rail of an app shell — brand mark, primary nav entries, and a footer slot for the current user. |
75	| `SidePanel` | core | A modal panel anchored to the right edge of the viewport, for a persistent secondary task alongside — but still blocking — the main page (details, a form, a filter builder). |
76	| `Switch` | core | Lets users toggle a single setting on or off, with the change taking effect immediately. |
77	| `Table` | core | Displays tabular data edge-to-edge — rows and columns of related records, e.g. |
78	| `Textarea` | core | Lets users enter multi-line free-form text. |
79	| `Toast` | core | A Sonner-style stacking notification, fixed to the top-right corner, triggered imperatively (toast.success('Saved')) from anywhere — not tied to a piece of UI state the consumer renders conditionally, unlike Modal/SidePanel. |
80	| `Tooltip` | core | Reveals a short, non-interactive text label for whatever it wraps, on hover or keyboard focus — identifies an ambiguous control (an icon-only button, an avatar) without adding permanent visible text. |
81	| `TopBar` | layout | The fixed-height chrome bar at the top of a page — search, quick actions, and the current user, always in the same place. |
82	<!-- helix:component-inventory:end -->
83	
84	## Component hierarchy (enforce this order)
85	
86	```
87	1. Helix core (@helixds/react)  ← always check first
88	2. Custom component             ← add comment: // [CUSTOM] reason
89	```
90	
91	Helix components are built directly on native HTML elements — there is no primitive library
92	underneath to reach for. If a Helix component doesn't exist yet, file a request.
93	
94	## Token usage
95	
96	Use Helix semantic tokens, never Tailwind primitives directly:
97	
98	```css
99	/* ✅ correct */
100	color: var(--helix-color-text-neutral);
101	background: var(--helix-color-fill-primary);
102	
103	/* ❌ wrong */
104	color: #1a1a1a;
105	background: blue-600;
106	```
107	
108	TypeScript constants are also available:
109	```ts
110	import { tokens } from '@helixds/tokens';
111	tokens.color.fill.primary; // '#1d4ed8'
112	```
113	
114	## Lint while you write
115	
116	`@helixds/eslint-plugin` catches the mistakes agents make most — an invented import path
117	(`@helixds/react` → `@helixds/react`), anti-synonym props and values (`onPress` → `onClick`,
118	`size="md"` → `size="m"`), raw colors (`#1d4ed8` → the semantic token with that color) and native
119	controls (`<button>` → `Button`). Run `pnpm lint` (or `npx eslint --fix <file>`) after writing UI code;
120	the editor shows the same warnings live. See `packages/eslint-plugin/README.md`.
121	
122	## Props vocabulary
123	
124	Use the canonical prop names below. Anti-synonyms are rejected by CI.
125	
126	| ✅ Use       | ❌ Never    | Notes                          |
127	|-------------|------------|--------------------------------|
128	| `variant`   | `type`     | Visual style selector          |
129	| `size`      | `scale`    | `xs s m l xl`                  |
130	| `isLoading`   | `loading`| Boolean authored state         |
131	| `disabled`  | `isDisabled`| Boolean authored state        |
132	| `danger`    | `error`    | Destructive variant name       |
133	| `current`   | `active`   | Navigation selected state      |
134	| `onClick`   | `onPress`  | Primary action handler         |
135	| `label`     | `title`, `name` | Accessible text          |
136	## Agent Readiness & Governance (Can it? Should it? May it?)
137	
138	When an AI agent makes design or implementation decisions using Helix, it must validate three levels of readiness:
139	
140	1. **Can it? (Mechanical Readiness)**:
141	   - Does the generated code compile and use valid tokens (`var(--helix-color-...)`)?
142	   - Are canonical props (`onClick`, `variant`, `expanded`) used according to component contracts?
143	   - Query Helix via CLI (`pnpm helix component <Name>`) or contracts to fetch machine-readable props and types.
144	
145	2. **Should it? (Design Judgment Readiness)**:
146	   - Does the usage respect `neverUseFor` anti-patterns documented in the component contract?
147	   - Does it preserve accessibility contracts (WCAG AA, focus trapping, aria semantics)?
148	   - Are responsive constraints and layout components (`AppShell`, `TopBar`, `SideNav`) respected?
149	
150	3. **May it? (Authority & Governance Readiness)**:
151	   - **Consuming apps**: Agents MAY use core Helix components and create local custom components flagged with `// [CUSTOM] reason`.
152	   - **Boundary Enforcement**: Agents MAY NOT alter shared token CSS variables directly (`style={{ color: '#xxx' }}`), override internal padding/height tokens, or redefine component prop contracts.
153	   - **Escalation**: If a requested UI pattern cannot be achieved with existing Helix components or local composition, the agent MUST flag it for human review or file a request for Helix DS.
154	
155	## AI context installation
156	
157	## Helix MCP tools (preferred when your client supports MCP)
158	
159	The repo registers a `helix` MCP server (`.mcp.json`, `pnpm helix:mcp`). Use its tools instead of reading
160	files or shelling out:
161	
162	1. `helix_list_components` — check Helix has the component before building anything.
163	2. `helix_get_contract` — exact props, accessibility and governance for the component you're using.
164	3. `helix_search_tokens` — the token for a concept ("danger background", "subtle text"); never hardcode.
165	4. `helix_validate_snippet` — run your JSX through it before writing the file; apply `fixedCode`, then
166	   fix what's left in `remainingAfterFix`.
167	
168	## Querying Helix from a terminal
169	
170	When an agent has shell access, use the read-only CLI to discover the exact Helix guidance needed
171	instead of searching source files broadly. It reads the same contracts, tokens, and patterns used by
172	the design system — it does not maintain a second copy of the documentation.
173	
174	```bash
175	pnpm helix search "confirmation dialog" --json
176	pnpm helix component Modal --json
177	pnpm helix token color.fill.primary-interactive-default --json
178	pnpm helix pattern empty-state --json
179	```
180	
181	Use `pnpm helix batch --command "component Button" --command "token color.fill.primary-interactive-default" --json`
182	when several lookups are needed. If no shell is available, consult `contracts/manifest.json`, the
183	specific component contract, and `.ai/maps/` directly.
184	
185	When no Helix component covers what you need, scaffold the custom one instead of writing it from
186	scratch — it comes with the `// [CUSTOM] reason:` header, semantic tokens, an accessible base and a
187	Storybook story whose `play` function is its first test:
188	
189	```bash
190	pnpm helix scaffold:custom UsageMeter --reason "Helix has no meter component" --dir src/custom/UsageMeter
191	```
192	
193	To install Helix AI context in your project:
194	
195	From a clone of the Helix repo:
196	
197	```bash
198	pnpm setup:ai [target-dir] [--dry-run]
199	```
200	
201	This copies AGENTS.md into your project (never overwriting a hand-edited one — it flags
202	a conflict instead) and writes a pointer file for whichever AI tool directories it finds
203	already in your project (`.cursor/rules/helix.mdc`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`).
204	Safe to run more than once. See `scripts/setup-ai.mjs` for exactly what it does and does
205	not touch.
206	
207	## Common mistakes (seen in real eval runs)
208	
209	These came up when an agent was asked to build with Helix without reading the contracts first
210	(`pnpm eval:generate`). Check them before writing the code:
211	
212	- **Toast needs `<Toast />` mounted once** (near the app root). `toast.success(...)` only queues the
213	  notification; with no `<Toast />` nothing appears (Helix logs a console warning). Signature:
214	  `toast.success(label, description?)` — the description can also be `{ description }`.
215	- **TopBar's slots are `start` and `end`** — not `search`/`actions`, not `left`/`right`.
216	- **Canonical prop names only** — `onClick` (not `onPress`), `expanded` (not `open`/`isOpen`),
217	  `label` (not `title`/`name`), `checked` (not `active`/`selected`), `current` (not `active`). Full list:
218	  `.ai/maps/prop-map.md`.
219	- **Icons by reference** — `icon={IconPlus}`, never `icon={<IconPlus />}`, never a raw `<IconPlus />`.
220	
221	## What agents should NOT do
222	
223	- Use `style={{ color: '#xxx' }}` — always use token CSS variables
224	- Create a `<div>` grid without importing a Helix layout component first
225	- Use `onPress` — prefer `onClick` (prop-map canonical)
226	- Use Figma prop names directly — they may not match Helix contracts
227

```ts
import { tokens } from '@helixds/tokens';
tokens.color.fill.primary; // '#1d4ed8'
```

## Lint while you write

`@helixds/eslint-plugin` catches the mistakes agents make most — an invented import path
(`@helixds/react` → `@helixds/react`), anti-synonym props and values (`onPress` → `onClick`,
`size="md"` → `size="m"`), raw colors (`#1d4ed8` → the semantic token with that color) and native
controls (`<button>` → `Button`). Run `pnpm lint` (or `npx eslint --fix <file>`) after writing UI code;
the editor shows the same warnings live. See `packages/eslint-plugin/README.md`.

## Props vocabulary

Use the canonical prop names below. Anti-synonyms are rejected by CI.

| ✅ Use       | ❌ Never    | Notes                          |
|-------------|------------|--------------------------------|
| `variant`   | `type`     | Visual style selector          |
| `size`      | `scale`    | `xs s m l xl`                  |
| `isLoading`   | `loading`| Boolean authored state         |
| `disabled`  | `isDisabled`| Boolean authored state        |
| `danger`    | `error`    | Destructive variant name       |
| `current`   | `active`   | Navigation selected state      |
| `onClick`   | `onPress`  | Primary action handler         |
| `label`     | `title`, `name` | Accessible text          |
## Agent Readiness & Governance (Can it? Should it? May it?)

When an AI agent makes design or implementation decisions using Helix, it must validate three levels of readiness:

1. **Can it? (Mechanical Readiness)**:
   - Does the generated code compile and use valid tokens (`var(--helix-color-...)`)?
   - Are canonical props (`onClick`, `variant`, `expanded`) used according to component contracts?
   - Query Helix via CLI (`pnpm helix component <Name>`) or contracts to fetch machine-readable props and types.

2. **Should it? (Design Judgment Readiness)**:
   - Does the usage respect `neverUseFor` anti-patterns documented in the component contract?
   - Does it preserve accessibility contracts (WCAG AA, focus trapping, aria semantics)?
   - Are responsive constraints and layout components (`AppShell`, `TopBar`, `SideNav`) respected?

3. **May it? (Authority & Governance Readiness)**:
   - **Consuming apps**: Agents MAY use core Helix components and create local custom components flagged with `// [CUSTOM] reason`.
   - **Boundary Enforcement**: Agents MAY NOT alter shared token CSS variables directly (`style={{ color: '#xxx' }}`), override internal padding/height tokens, or redefine component prop contracts.
   - **Escalation**: If a requested UI pattern cannot be achieved with existing Helix components or local composition, the agent MUST flag it for human review or file a request for Helix DS.

## AI context installation

## Helix MCP tools (preferred when your client supports MCP)

The repo registers a `helix` MCP server (`.mcp.json`, `pnpm helix:mcp`). Use its tools instead of reading
files or shelling out:

1. `helix_list_components` — check Helix has the component before building anything.
2. `helix_get_contract` — exact props, accessibility and governance for the component you're using.
3. `helix_search_tokens` — the token for a concept ("danger background", "subtle text"); never hardcode.
4. `helix_validate_snippet` — run your JSX through it before writing the file; apply `fixedCode`, then
   fix what's left in `remainingAfterFix`.

## Querying Helix from a terminal

When an agent has shell access, use the read-only CLI to discover the exact Helix guidance needed
instead of searching source files broadly. It reads the same contracts, tokens, and patterns used by
the design system — it does not maintain a second copy of the documentation.

```bash
pnpm helix search "confirmation dialog" --json
pnpm helix component Modal --json
pnpm helix token color.fill.primary-interactive-default --json
pnpm helix pattern empty-state --json
```

Use `pnpm helix batch --command "component Button" --command "token color.fill.primary-interactive-default" --json`
when several lookups are needed. If no shell is available, consult `contracts/manifest.json`, the
specific component contract, and `.ai/maps/` directly.

When no Helix component covers what you need, scaffold the custom one instead of writing it from
scratch — it comes with the `// [CUSTOM] reason:` header, semantic tokens, an accessible base and a
Storybook story whose `play` function is its first test:

```bash
pnpm helix scaffold:custom UsageMeter --reason "Helix has no meter component" --dir src/custom/UsageMeter
```

To install Helix AI context in your project:

From a clone of the Helix repo:

```bash
pnpm setup:ai [target-dir] [--dry-run]
```

This copies AGENTS.md into your project (never overwriting a hand-edited one — it flags
a conflict instead) and writes a pointer file for whichever AI tool directories it finds
already in your project (`.cursor/rules/helix.mdc`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`).
Safe to run more than once. See `scripts/setup-ai.mjs` for exactly what it does and does
not touch.

## Common mistakes (seen in real eval runs)

These came up when an agent was asked to build with Helix without reading the contracts first
(`pnpm eval:generate`). Check them before writing the code:

- **Toast needs `<Toast />` mounted once** (near the app root). `toast.success(...)` only queues the
  notification; with no `<Toast />` nothing appears (Helix logs a console warning). Signature:
  `toast.success(label, description?)` — the description can also be `{ description }`.
- **TopBar's slots are `start` and `end`** — not `search`/`actions`, not `left`/`right`.
- **Canonical prop names only** — `onClick` (not `onPress`), `expanded` (not `open`/`isOpen`),
  `label` (not `title`/`name`), `checked` (not `active`/`selected`), `current` (not `active`). Full list:
  `.ai/maps/prop-map.md`.
- **Icons by reference** — `icon={IconPlus}`, never `icon={<IconPlus />}`, never a raw `<IconPlus />`.

## What agents should NOT do

- Use `style={{ color: '#xxx' }}` — always use token CSS variables
- Create a `<div>` grid without importing a Helix layout component first
- Use `onPress` — prefer `onClick` (prop-map canonical)
- Use Figma prop names directly — they may not match Helix contracts

Done! I've implemented the invite team member form with comprehensive validation and error handling. Here's what the form does:

**Form features:**
- **Email field** – validates that it's not empty and matches a valid email format
- **Role field** – dropdown to select from Admin, Editor, or Viewer
- **Validation** – runs on form submission; both fields are required
- **Error messages** – displayed directly below the field that failed validation in red, with specific guidance (e.g., "Please enter a valid email address")
- **Accessibility** – uses `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby` so screen readers announce validation errors to users
- **Success feedback** – shows a brief success message after submission, then resets the form

The form uses Helix components (Button, Card, Input, Select) and semantic tokens for colors (`--helix-color-text-danger` for errors). When users try to submit with missing or invalid data, they'll see exactly which field needs attention and why.
